messages.subject: Storing eigecomponents in nimble
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to embed an eigendecomposition of a fixed n x n matrix (Sigma) within my nimble model string. The goal is to compute the eigenvectors and values of the matrix at each iteration of an MCMC algorithm. My nimble model builds properly when I perform two separate eigendecompositions of the same n x n matrix. That is, one to extract the eigenvectors and another for the eigenvalues. 

In order to manage the computational costs, is it possible to run just one eigendecomposition and store both eigencomponents in a nimbleList or an eigenNimbleList?  Though the help manual provides some related code (Section 13.2.1 - Using eigen and svd in nimbleFunctions), I haven't been able to successfully apply this to the problem at hand. Any tips or pointers would be much appreciated!

Attached, please find the toy example R file, and the pertinent model string is as follows:

model_string <- nimbleCode({

  # Data Model - Poisson Likelihood
  for(i in 1:n){
    Z[i] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[i])
    lambda[i] <- exp(W[i]+XB[i])
  }
  
  XB[1:n]<-beta1*X[,1] + beta2*X[,2]

  # Process Model
  W[1:n] <- U[1:n,1:n]%*%(D[1:n,1:n]%*%delta[1:n])

  # Currently requires two eigendecompositions of the n x n matrix Sigma (Sigma is fixed in the toy example)
  # Is it possible to perform on eigendecomposition and store the eigenvectors and eigenvalues in a single object
  U[1:n,1:n]  <- eigen(Sigma[1:n,1:n], symmetric = TRUE)$vectors[1:n,1:n] 
  D[1:n,1:n] <- diag(sqrt(eigen(Sigma[1:n,1:n], symmetric = TRUE)$values[1:n]))
  
  for(i in 1:n) {
    delta[i] ~ dnorm(mean=0,  var=1)  
  }
  
  # Parameter Model
  beta1 ~  dnorm(0, sd=sqrt(100))
  beta2 ~  dnorm(0, sd=sqrt(100))
})

Thank you very much! 

Best, 
Ben

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Storing eigecomponents in nimble
parts:
Hi Ben,

Good question. It's not directly possible in model code because one can't use a list or other complicated data structure in model code. However you can do it by writing a user-defined function. This user defined function would compute the eigendecomposition and return the result as a (n x (n+1)) or ((n+1) x n) matrix, where the extra column or row contains the eigenvalues. You would then use subsets of this matrix appropriately in your model code.

Your model code would look something like this:

W[1:n] <- (U[1:n,1:n]%*%(sqrt(U[1:n,n+1])*delta[1:n]))[ , 1]
U[1:n, 1:(n+1)] <- myEigenDecomp(Sigma[1:n, 1:n])

where `myEigenDecomp` is a user-defined function. For more info on writing a user-defined function you can look in the manual. For an example of a user-defined function, please see: https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/gaussian_process.html. The latter plus the material in Sec. 13.2.1 that you've already seen may be sufficient for you.

Side note: You need the [,1] at the end because the result of the matrix multiplication is a (one-column) matrix and to assign to a vector you need to "subset" it.

messages.subject: Re: Storing eigecomponents in nimble
parts:
Hi Chris, 

Thank you so much for taking a look at this. I followed your suggestion, and it seems to have done the trick! 

I basically created a user-defined function (outside of the model code) that returns a matrix comprised of the eigenvectors and eigenvalues (last column). Then I embedded it into the model code as you advised. Thank you again. 

The user-defined function and model code is:

eigDecomp<-nimbleFunction(     
  run = function(sigma = double(2)) {
    returnType(double(2))
    n=dim(sigma)[1]
    result<-matrix(nrow = n, ncol = n+1, init = FALSE)
    eigFull <- eigen(sigma,symmetric = TRUE)
    result[1:n,1:n]<-eigFull$vectors[1:n,1:n]
    result[1:n,n+1]<-eigFull$values[1:n]
    return(result)
  })

# Nimble Model

model_string <- nimbleCode({
  
  # Data Model - Poisson Likelihood
  for(i in 1:n){
    Z[i] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[i])
    lambda[i] <- exp(W[i]+XB[i])
  }
  
  XB[1:n]<-beta1*X[,1] + beta2*X[,2]
  
  # Process Model

for(i in 1:n) {
    delta[i] ~ dnorm(mean=0,  var=1) 
  }
  
  # Parameter Model
  beta1 ~  dnorm(0, sd=sqrt(100))
  beta2 ~  dnorm(0, sd=sqrt(100))
})
